{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My husband organized surprise parties for me every year—elaborate affairs with catering and decorations. I hate surprises and have severe social anxiety. But his joy in planning them is so pure that I've performed delight for eleven years. He still doesn't know each party triggers a migraine.

CANDIDATE A:
My best friend believes we share a love of hiking. I'm terrified of heights and trails exhaust me. But those hikes are when she opens up about her struggles, and I can't bear to lose that intimacy. I've spent fifteen years pretending to love something I dread.

CANDIDATE B:
My husband organized surprise parties for me every year. Last year I finally told him I actually don't enjoy surprises—I prefer knowing the plan. He was surprised but understood. This year he involved me in planning, and I enjoyed the party more than ever.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:45"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both stories involve a person sacrificing their own comfort and preferences to maintain a relationship and intimacy with someone they care about, despite the personal toll it takes."}
